images.title: Hidden depths
images.caption: Ice on Abraham Lake in Alberta, Canada
images.desc: Dawn's first light is reflected on the frozen surface of Abraham Lake, framed by peaks of the Rocky Mountains. In winter, this picturesque lake in Alberta is famous for its frozen bubbles of methane gas, trapped beneath the ice. Strong winds keep the surface clear of snow, offering winter-long views. Come spring, when the ice thaws, the gas escapes into the atmosphere. Despite its natural beauty, the lake is a human-made reservoir, created in 1972 when the Bighorn Dam was built on the North Saskatchewan River. Its icy beauty in winter and turquoise waters in summer make it a popular photography spot all year round.

images.title: Architecture without an architect
images.caption: North Window, Arches National Park, Moab, Utah
images.desc: On November 12, Arches National Park marks the anniversary of its designation as a national park in 1971. Just north of Moab, Utah, the high-desert park is home to more than 2,000 natural sandstone arches—the densest concentration of arches in the world. Today's image, North Window, is one of the best-known formations in the park's Windows Section, where towering fins, openings, and sculpted sandstone create a landscape that looks almost architectural.

images.title: Licensed to chill
images.caption: Aerial view of Rose Island, The Bahamas
images.desc: From above, Rose Island looks like a brushstroke of green surrounded by every shade of blue. Just three miles east of Paradise Island in The Bahamas, this slender cay trades busy roads and city blocks for sandy shores, shallow waters, and an inland lagoon. Its peaceful appearance comes with a touch of movie drama. Rose Island was used as a filming location for the 1965 James Bond adventure 'Thunderball,' including the explosive destruction of the Disco Volante.

images.title: Where art finds its rhythm
images.caption: Historic district of Triana, Seville, Spain
images.desc: Cross the Guadalquivir River in Seville, the capital of Spain's Andalusia region, and the city's rhythm seems to change. On the other side lies Triana, a colorful neighborhood where ceramics, flamenco, and local traditions are woven into everyday life. Since the 19th century, the Isabel II Bridge, also known as the Triana Bridge, has connected the neighborhood to Seville's historic center.

images.caption: National Bison Day
images.desc: When the going gets tough, the bison gets grazing. National Bison Day celebrates the North American mammal that can weigh up to 2,000 pounds yet sprint at 35 mph. Observed on the first Saturday of November, the day honors the bovine that became the United States' national mammal in 2016.

images.title: A green tunnel through Maui
images.caption: Bamboo forest, Haleakalā National Park, Maui, Hawaii
images.desc: A volcano, a rainforest, and a bamboo grove? Haleakalā National Park on Maui has all three. Spanning Maui from its 10,023-foot summit to the coast, the park protects landscapes that change dramatically with elevation, rainfall, and temperature. It was established in 1916 as part of Hawaii National Park and became its own national park in 1961. The name Haleakalā translates to 'House of the Sun,' reflecting the Hawaiian mo'olelo of Māui capturing the sun to lengthen the day.
